title: Story structure: context, conflict, evidence and recommendation

videos.script: Every story you have ever followed has the same skeleton. Somebody is somewhere. Something goes wrong. Things happen. It ends. {{skeleton}} A presentation of an analysis has that skeleton too, and it has four parts. Context, conflict, evidence and recommendation. {{four}} Context is what the room already agrees on. Conflict is the gap that makes your finding worth eleven minutes. {{context}} Evidence is the fewest facts that make the gap believable. Recommendation is what you want done, and it is where the story stops. {{evidence}} This lesson takes Faro's finding and builds it into those four parts. The surprise is where the conflict comes from. It comes from Sandra's number, the one that seemed to say nothing was wrong. {{faro}}
